description:
FILED s536j (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08): the part of #4302 that PPI batch 8 MEASURED and did not ship.  Catalogue docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §65, registry row 65 (fixed_in undef), report rows on the branch inside a PCL §65 TODO block (branch pcl-s536j ae78574f / docs/ppi-bug-report.t, three rows + one control).

THE PPI SIDE.  vendor/PPI/lib/PPI/Tokenizer.pm `new` (line ~209): `$self->{source} =~ s/(?:\015{1,2}\012|\015|\012)/\n/g;` then `split /(?<=\n)/`.  Measured (s536j): dropping the rewrite and splitting on LF only fails exactly ONE row of PPI's suite -- t/06_round_trip.t 2146 "t/perf.t: Round trip was successful" (t/perf.t has CR LF line ends, and the test normalizes its expected text with the same regex: t/06_round_trip.t:76; t/08_regression.t:270 does it too).  So the rewrite is PPI behaviour its own tests ASSERT: keeping the CRs is either a behaviour change (the round-trip test then compares exact bytes -- more faithful, an upstream decision) or a new Document / Tokenizer attribute (e.g. `PPI::Document->new(\$src, keep_line_endings => 1)`, threaded through PPI::Lexer->lex_source to PPI::Tokenizer->new) that PCL passes.  Either way PPI's here-doc terminator test (Token/HereDoc.pm _is_terminator: `$line eq "TERM\n"`) must accept `TERM\r\n` (perl does, file and eval).

PERL'S RULE (probed 5.40.3, scratch/s536j/p/cr1.pl cr2.pl cr3.pl, mkcr.pl writes them): toke.c without PERL_STRICT_CR.
  * a source FILE (read line by line): the CR before the LF at the end of each line INSIDE a multi-line string / quote-like literal becomes LF (S_scan_str); a here-doc body: CR LF -> LF and a lone CR -> LF (S_scan_heredoc); a CR in the middle of a line (a single-line literal) is KEPT; the __DATA__ / __END__ section is read raw (CRs KEPT).
  * a STRING EVAL (one buffer): literals KEEP every CR (`length eval "q{a\r\nb}"` is 4); here-doc bodies still convert (`eval "<<E;\r\nx\r\nE\r\n"` is "x\n").
  PPI's rewrite matches perl for file-mode multi-line literals and every here-doc; it is WRONG for: a CR inside a single-line literal (file and eval), every literal of a string eval, and the __DATA__ section.

THE PCL SIDE once PPI keeps the CRs: (a) here-doc bodies: CR LF and lone CR -> LF (both modes) -- PPI::Token::HereDoc's `_heredoc` lines can be edited in place; (b) FILE mode only: CR LF -> LF inside quote-like / regex literals -- NOT by set_content (PPI's quote tokens keep section offsets into their content), but at the SOURCE: in file mode, before the parse, rewrite CR LF -> LF on every line BEFORE the data section's separator line (the separator's line from a first tokenization; only files that hold a CR pay a second parse); (c) eval mode: nothing; (d) __DATA__ comes from PPI::Token::Data's content (Pl::Parser _process_element End/Data) and is then raw, as perl.

PREVALENCE: 2 of 2,158 files in the wide A/B list + corpus hold a CR (t/op/inccode.t one CR LF, t/re/bigfuzzy_not_utf8.t one lone CR); 0 of the 402 board files.  The known failure: Template-Toolkit-3.106-0 t/parser.t row 35 (`[% wintxt | replace("(\r\n){2,}", ...) %]`: TT's generated Perl carries the CR LF characters verbatim into a string EVAL, PCL's PPI rewrites them, the replace never matches).

BAR for the batch that takes it: PPI's suite plain + AUTHOR green (the round-trip row updated under the four-conjunct rule if the behaviour changes, or untouched with the attribute); the §65 report rows out of TODO; p/cr1-3.pl perl -> PCL identical; TT parser.t row 35 BEFORE -> AFTER; wide A/B (t/op/inccode.t, t/re/bigfuzzy_not_utf8.t the expected movers).


=== USER RULING (s538, 2026-11-11; paraphrased) ===
Rewriting the line endings of pure CODE is not a problem; inside STRINGS it probably should not happen.  So the design direction is settled: PPI keeps normalising CR LF / CR between tokens (code, comments, white space), and the CONTENT of a quote, a here-doc body and the __DATA__ / __END__ section keeps its bytes -- as far as perl itself keeps them.  The reviewing session probed perl 5.40.3 the same day (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s538/review/j/p4.pl): in a source FILE perl reads a CR LF pair as LF even inside q{} and a here-doc body (length 3 for q{a<CR><LF>b}), and keeps a lone CR in a string, every CR in an eval STRING and every CR in __DATA__.  The bar is perl, shape by shape: the fix keeps what perl keeps, not every CR.  Owner: the next PPI batch (the PPI attribute + PCL halves designed in this task).
subject: PPI (PCL's branch) rewrites every CR LF / lone CR of the source to LF -- the rest of #4302 MEASURED (s536j): one PPI test asserts the rewrite; perl's CR rules differ by file / eval mode; the PPI attribute + PCL halves designed, not shipped
